- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, expect overshoot or overconfidence in early price spikes; adjust downward by 5–10% for the next 5–7 days.
- If supply net is heavily negative (e.g., -20+), model forecasts often lag the true price drop; apply a 3–5 day lag correction with a 10–15% downward bias in the first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 20–30% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, expect mean reversion; cap upward trend at 1–2% above recent low.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for the first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment shifts; align forecast slope with sentiment direction change within 3–5 days.
- For auctions with high supply net, model often underestimates price drop; apply 5–10% downward bias for 3–5 days post-auction.
